static.mainsAngle: Evaluate whether India's consolidated labour codes have expanded or diluted worker protection, especially for informal and gig workers.

static.topic: Automation, AI and Employment Displacement
static.syllabusNode: Economy — Inclusive Growth & Employment; Science & Technology — Effects on Society
static.whatIsIt: The debate over whether artificial intelligence and automation destroy more jobs than they create, and what policy responses — reskilling, social protection, transition support — are needed for displaced workers.
static.background: Successive waves of mechanisation and digitalisation have raised similar concerns; the current phase is distinguished by AI applications in services, back-office and customer-facing roles, which are significant employers in India's IT-BPM sector. The Conversation cites Qantas cutting 850 jobs alongside an outsourcing agreement with Accenture as an illustration of AI being invoked in layoff decisions.
static.socioEconomic: India's demographic dividend depends on absorbing a large young workforce; automation in labour-intensive and services sectors could compress entry-level hiring, making skills and social security policy more urgent.
static.whyInNews: AI is increasingly cited by firms as a reason for mass layoffs, prompting debate on fair transition mechanisms for affected workers.
static.wayForward: Invest in continuous reskilling and lifelong learning, expand portable social security, and design adjustment or transition support so that technological gains are shared rather than borne entirely by displaced workers.

static.background: The collegium system evolved through the Three Judges Cases (1981, 1993, 1998). Kesavananda Bharati (1973) established the basic-structure doctrine. PILs expanded access to justice from the late 1970s. Article 32 (SC) and 226 (HC) provide writ jurisdiction.

static.topic: State politics, local body elections and Centre-State friction

static.background: Sarkaria (1983) and Punchhi (2007) Commissions examined the Centre-State balance. For Tamil Nadu, this translates into heightened water stress because the state's agriculture and domestic supplies depend heavily on monsoon rainfall and reservoir storage. The report warns that weak or erratic rainfall can reduce crop yields, shrink farm incomes and deepen rural distress. It situates the risk within a broader pattern where natural El Niño variability is compounded by anthropogenic climate change. static.topic: El Niño, Climate Variability and India's Climate Commitments
static.whatIsIt: El Niño is a naturally occurring climate pattern involving abnormal warming of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific; its impacts are being amplified by global warming. India's climate regime under the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement frames adaptation and mitigation commitments.
static.background: UNFCCC 1992; Kyoto Protocol 1997; Paris Agreement 2015; India targets net-zero by 2070 and 50% installed non-fossil capacity by 2030. CBDR-RC is the core equity principle; Loss & Damage fund was operationalised at COP28 (2023); India leads the International Solar Alliance (2015) and LiFE mission.
static.geography: Tamil Nadu is a coastal southern state; its agriculture and water supply depend heavily on the northeast monsoon and Cauvery basin reservoirs. El Niño can disrupt monsoon rainfall patterns, affecting delta agriculture.
static.socioEconomic: A large share of the population depends on agriculture; water stress can reduce yields, farm incomes and employment, worsening rural debt and migration.
static.whyInNews: INCOIS has indicated an 80–100% probability of the persistent El Niño phase continuing; Mongabay India warns this could deepen Tamil Nadu's water stress and threaten agriculture.
static.wayForward: Strengthen early warning, reservoir and groundwater management, crop diversification, micro-irrigation, climate-resilient seeds, and integrate El Niño advisories into state agriculture and water policy.

static.socioEconomic: Small and marginal farmers, tenant cultivators and agricultural labourers are most vulnerable to yield loss, income decline and debt. Water-intensive cropping raises sustainability concerns.
static.whyInNews: El Niño-linked water stress could reduce crop output and farm incomes in Tamil Nadu, renewing debate on MSP, procurement, crop diversification and safety nets.
static.wayForward: Promote millets, pulses and drought-tolerant varieties; expand micro-irrigation; strengthen crop insurance and procurement for diversified crops; manage groundwater and reservoir storage; integrate climate advisories with MSP and PDS planning.

static.background: The Gaza Strip has been under Israeli blockade since 2007, after Hamas took control there. Repeated rounds of conflict (2008-09, 2012, 2014, 2021) preceded the war that began in October 2023. Mediation by Qatar, Egypt and the United States produced successive ceasefire and hostage-release arrangements, including a phased framework that created redeployment lines and humanitarian pauses. Implementation has remained contested, with each side accusing the other of violations.

static.topic: UN Security Council and Multilateral Responses to West Asian Conflicts

static.whatIsIt: The UN Security Council, with 15 members (five permanent veto-wielding members and ten elected for two-year terms), is the primary body for international peace and security; its resolutions shape ceasefire, sanctions and humanitarian mandates in Gaza and the wider region.
static.background: The UN was founded in 1945; India is a founding member and one of the largest troop contributors to UN peacekeeping. The G4 (India, Brazil, Germany, Japan) campaigns for permanent seats, while the Intergovernmental Negotiations (IGN) on Security Council reform remain inconclusive. Repeated vetoes on West Asia resolutions have renewed calls for reform.
static.whyInNews: The Gaza ground operation and competing ceasefire-violation claims again spotlight the Security Council's paralysis and the debate on veto use and reform.
static.wayForward: Revitalised text-based IGN negotiations, restraint on the veto in mass-atrocity situations, and expansion of both permanent and elected categories.
